title: Replacing half of faculty-led examination-skills teaching with near-peer sessions: a cost-effectiveness analysis alongside a concurrent comparison
abstract: Objective: to estimate the incremental cost per additional student passing all examination-skills stations when four of eight faculty sessions are replaced by calibrated near-peer sessions. Design: cost-effectiveness analysis alongside allocation of 2027 tutorial groups by timetable block, school perspective. Results and conclusions will follow the May 2027 OSCE.
introduction: Near-peer teaching gives similar short-term performance in small studies and is cheaper per contact hour, but economic evaluations with fair comparisons are rare.
methods: Eighteen tutorial groups are allocated by timetable block. The effect measure is first-attempt pass on all examination-skills stations; costs come from finance records. Uncertainty is shown by bootstrap and acceptability curves.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present costs, pass proportions, the incremental ratio and acceptability curves.
discussion: The discussion will set the result against the retrieved randomised comparison and costing, and state what a second year of data would add.
limitations: One school, one year, allocation by timetable rather than randomisation, and imprecise effect estimates.
summary: CHEERS-structured draft with results left empty.
